papers.title: Multi-scale vision transformer model with UAV-based hyperspectral imagery for early identification of pine wilt disease infected trees
papers.authors: Hao Shi, Ruirui Zhang, Meixiang Chen, Huixiang Liu, Danzhu Zhang
papers.abstract: Pine Wilt Disease (PWD), caused by the pine wood nematode ( Bursaphelenchus xylophilus ), is a devastating forest disease characterized by rapid spread and high mortality. During its pathogenesis, the green attack and early stage are critical for disease control. However, RGB UAV images lack obvious visual features at these stages, which limits the accuracy of existing identification methods. This study aims to develop a Multi-Scale Vision Transformer Model specifically designed for UAV hyperspectral data. The primary objectives are to improve the identification capability for the green attack and early stages of PWD. To accurately capture subtle changes in the spectral and spatial features of pine trees during the green attack stage, an efficient spectral-spatial feature fusion module was designed. Meanwhile, an improved Gaussian self-attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the modeling of spectral differences between central pixels and their neighboring pixels. papers.title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
papers.authors: A. Suresh kumar, C. Rajan
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Smart Infrastructure and Environmental Sustainability
papers.abstract: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. papers.authors: Hugh Davies, Nick Dexter, Dion Maple, Paul Meek
papers.abstract: Context The difficulties of invasive predator management can be exacerbated by suboptimal monitoring data. Developing a cost-effective, operationally achievable and statistically robust monitoring program is therefore a key component of biodiversity conservation and management. Aims To explore options to better balance the survey effort, cost and statistical power of the red fox (Vulpes vulpes) monitoring program at Booderee National Park (BNP), south-eastern Australia. Methods We analysed existing camera-trap data over an 8-year period to estimate fox occupancy and detectability. We then conducted a power analysis to assess our ability to detect reductions in fox occupancy of varying magnitudes under six hypothetical monitoring scenarios with varying survey effort. We compared how statistical power varied among scenarios between seasons of high and low fox detectability (i.e. summer and spring respectively), and across three levels of initial occupancy (Ψ = 0.75, 0.50, 0.25). Annual costs were estimated for each hypothetical scenario as well as the current fox monitoring approach at BNP. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Arthropods communities in organic orchards and adjacent hedgerows on Terceira Island (Azores, Portugal): a dataset supporting biological control research
papers.authors: Sophie Wallon, António Domingues, Alejandra Ros‐Prieto, Sébastien Lhoumeau, David João Horta Lopes
papers.abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. Under the scope of the BIODIVERSA+ COMCHA project, we sampled arthropod assemblages in six orchards certified under the Organic Production System on Terceira Island, Azores, Portugal, comparing the orchard interior with adjacent hedgerows. Sampling was carried out in September 2025 and May 2026 using standardised active methods: SLAM traps (Sea, Land and Air Malaise), nocturnal Active Aerial Search, nocturnal foliage beating and diurnal foliage beating. papers.title: Toward evidence-based fish welfare regulation: policy lessons from Chile, Norway, and Scotland
papers.authors: Juan Antonio Valdés
papers.abstract: Aquaculture has become a major contributor to global food production, but its rapid expansion and intensification have increased concerns regarding the welfare of farmed fish. Although advances in welfare science have generated animal-based measures, operational welfare indicators, and increasingly sophisticated monitoring technologies, their incorporation into regulatory frameworks remains uneven. This review examines the evolution of fish welfare regulation and compares the regulatory approaches of Chile, Norway, and Scotland, three major salmon-producing jurisdictions representing distinct models of welfare governance. The analysis distinguishes between legislation that directly establishes welfare obligations and sanitary, environmental, biosecurity, and production regulations that indirectly influence welfare determinants. Chile combines explicit legal recognition of fish welfare with an extensive sanitary and environmental regulatory architecture, although standardized animal-based welfare assessment, intervention criteria, and welfare-specific auditing remain limited. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.abstract: Campylobacter is a constant concern in ensuring food safety, as it is one of the most common pathogens in food. The main source of Campylobacter species in food is poultry meat, and the primary production of this meat is a critical point where measures need to be taken to reduce its presence in the food chain. Therefore, poultry slaughterhouses are recognized as places where it is necessary to implement measures to control and reduce the number of Campylobacter spp. Food business operators are obliged to ensure greater hygiene on the slaughter line, through the inspection of equipment for each step of slaughter and the application of regular cleaning protocols. Continuous monitoring of the presence and abundance of Campylobacter spp. on the slaughter line provides data on the validity of hygiene control measures in the slaughterhouse, as well as the data needed to assess the microbiological risk in poultry meat. Monitoring the presence of Campylobacter spp. in poultry slaughterhouses is a basic activity that is necessary for taking measures to reduce contamination, improve microbiological safety in poultry processing and thus improve the food safety system as a whole. papers.title: Comparative Assessment of Climate Change Impacts and Farmers’ Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices in Tropical Crops Production Systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines
papers.authors: Phoebe Nemenzo-Calica, Marsha M. Pinaca, Grace B. Flores, Junas R. Acdog, Mark Ronald S. Manseguiao
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Tropical Crop Science
papers.abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens tropical crop production through erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events that reduce crop productivity and disrupt farm management. This study assessed climate change impacts and farmers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) across banana, cassava, and mixed-cropping systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines. A total of 450 farmers were surveyed using a structured questionnaire, and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). Banana farmers perceived the greatest climate change impacts (mean = 4.35), followed by cassava (4.05) and mixed-crop farmers (3.98). Across all systems, farmers demonstrated moderate to high knowledge (3.55–3.85) and positive attitudes (3.70–4.10) toward climate change adaptation, yet adaptation practices remained only moderate (3.50–3.75). Major climate-related challenges included erratic rainfall, prolonged drought, flooding, increasing pest and disease incidence, and declining crop yields. papers.authors: Isaac Osei‐Bonsu, Augustine Antwi-Boasiako, Michael Wiafe‐Kwagyan, Eric Owusu Danquah, Harry Okyere
papers.abstract: Climate change is reshaping the risk landscape of food systems by altering pathogen ecology, contaminant dynamics, crop and livestock productivity, water availability, and supply-chain stability. Rising temperatures and shifting precipitation patterns influence the prevalence, distribution, and virulence of foodborne and vector-borne pathogens, mycotoxins, and harmful algal blooms. Extreme weather events, including droughts, floods, storms, and heatwaves, can degrade soils, mobilize chemical contaminants, and compromise irrigation water and fresh produce quality. These can also damage infrastructure, disrupt supply chains and cold-chain integrity, and increase postharvest losses. This chapter examines these interconnected mechanisms through insights from predictive microbiology, toxicology, climate and crop modelling, remote sensing, and risk assessment. It presents a conceptual framework linking climatic drivers and environmental stressors to production, processing, distribution, consumption, food safety, nutrition and resilience outcomes. papers.abstract: Wild boar (Sus scrofa) is one of the most widely distributed wild ungulates, and its populations are increasing and expanding globally due to socioeconomic change, reduced predator pressure, and climate warming. Rooting, a characteristic foraging behavior in which wild boars overturn litter, vegetation, and soil, is a major disturbance in forest ecosystems and can alter soil properties, biotic communities, ecosystem processes, and ecosystem services. In this literature review, we synthesize current knowledge of wild boar rooting in forest ecosystems. We first summarize the drivers of rooting regimes. We then review rooting-induced changes in soil physical and chemical properties, the community structure of soil microbes, invertebrates, and understory vegetation, as well as ecosystem processes and functions, including carbon and nitrogen dynamics and forest regeneration. We also discuss methodological challenges in quantifying rooting and their implications for cross-study comparisons. By reviewing previous studies, we found that both rooting regimes and their ecological impacts are highly context dependent. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.authors: Szandra László

papers.abstract: Psychomotor alterations may represent an important symptom dimension of major psychiatric disorders. Actigraphy enables the objective assessment of motor activity and rest–activity rhythms in naturalistic settings. The aim of this dissertation was to investigate psychomotor patterns associated with the schizophrenia and bipolar spectra using detailed actigraphic feature extraction and machine learning methods. The dissertation is based on two cross-sectional studies. In the first study, we examined the actigraphic profiles of individuals without a psychiatric diagnosis who were characterised by cyclothymic temperament (CFG) or positive schizotypal traits (PSF), compared with controls. In the second study, using two independent databases, we analysed the model patterns of the PSF group and individuals with chronic schizophrenia (CS), each relative to their respective control group. Models based on combinations of detailed actigraphic features distinguished the psychometric groups from controls more accurately than models based on simple activity measures. papers.title: Non-target effect of fungicides on root endophytic fungus Microdochium bolleyi in barley
papers.authors: Pavel Matušinský, Zuzana Antalová, Tereza Šlajsová, Natálie Jarošová, Dominik Bleša
papers.abstract: Abstract Fungicides are widely used in crop protection to control phytopathogenic fungi, yet their effects on non-target microorganisms inhabiting plant tissues remain poorly understood. Endophytic fungi are components of the plant microbiome, but assessing how fungicide applications influence their colonisation is challenging because these interactions are often asymptomatic. In this study, a simplified barley- Microdochium bolleyi model system was used to investigate the effects of fungicide exposure on endophytic colonisation. In vitro sensitivity assays revealed differences among fungicides, with prothioconazole showing the highest activity against sixteen M. bolleyi isolates (EC 50 = 0.11 µg mL⁻¹), followed by fluxapyroxad (0.31 µg mL⁻¹), mefentrifluconazole (0.37 µg mL⁻¹), and azoxystrobin (0.50 µg mL⁻¹). Based on these results, prothioconazole was selected for greenhouse experiments. Application of this systemic fungicide as either a seed dressing or foliar treatment significantly reduced root colonisation by M. bolleyi in barley. papers.title: Plant resilience: harnessing bioactive compounds for sustainable disease protection
papers.authors: Muhammad Zunair Latif, Miaomiao Deng, Naila Asghar, Lingguang Kong, Sumaira Kousar
papers.abstract: Plants have evolved complex phytochemical and immune defense mechanisms in response to pathogen invasion. Plants deploy phytochemical defense system-signaling molecules, secondary metabolites, antimicrobial proteins and peptides-to mitigate the pathogens they encounter. Pathogens have developed strategies-effector proteins, efflux pumps and detoxification mechanisms-to manipulate or overcome plant defenses. This review offers insights into how these bioactive compounds are biosynthesized and activated following pathogen recognition. We provide an overview of the dynamic crosstalk between PTI and ETI and their role in optimizing plant defense. Additionally, we discuss the potential of advanced genetic engineering approaches, nanocarrier-mediated elicitor delivery, and microbiome engineering to enhance these natural defenses. Finally, we address the technical bottlenecks of engineering plant immunity and provide a roadmap for future research directions. This review provides a stronger mechanistic foundation for breeding crops with durable, broad-spectrum resilience for sustainable crop protection.

papers.title: Real time small target fire detection in photovoltaic plants using attention enhanced multiscale fusion
papers.authors: Wei Guo, Xiujun Meng, Jingcheng Wang, Chunhui Cai, Haojie Cui
papers.abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power plants concentrate flammable polymers and arc-prone electrical components, making early fire detection a safety-critical condition-monitoring task. Yet incipient fires appear as small, weakly contrasted smoke or flame, while specular reflections from glossy module surfaces fabricate fire-like cues, jointly degrading conventional detectors. We cast this as an applied computational-intelligence problem and propose PVFire-YOLO, a real-time neural detection framework. A patch-aware parallel attention block amplifies weak small-target responses against reflective backgrounds; a gather-and-distribute neck performs intelligent information fusion across four feature-pyramid levels to close the semantic gap of conventional necks; and a four-scale adaptive spatial feature-fusion head learns per-pixel scale weights, adding a high-resolution branch for sub-100-pixel targets. To enable training and evaluation, we built PV-Fire, the first annotated flame-and-smoke corpus with a PV-specific background distribution. papers.authors: Bhavnah Komul Kalidin
papers.abstract: Marine invasive species introduced by ship biofouling threatens Small Island Developing States (SIDS). Using a mixed-methods approach involving policy reviews, surveys, semi-structured interviews, and documentary analysis this thesis evaluates SIDS’ preparedness. It identifies systemic deficiencies and provides practical solutions to strengthen SIDS capacity and enhance global biosecurity equity and resilience.

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: This study aimed to investigate the concentrations of heavy metals bound to airborne Particulate Matter (PM) in high-traffic districts of Tehran, Iran, and to determine the carcinogenic risk and Hazard Quotient (HQ) of these metals using a descriptive-applied method. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). After extracting the metals from fiberglass filters by acid digestion based on the ASTM (the American Society for Testing and Materials method), the concentrations of heavy metals were determined by an Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) device. The human health risk was evaluated according to the US EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) standard method. The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.title: Application of medical gases in prevention and treatment of electromagnetic radiation injury.
papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. Its symptoms often resemble nutrient deficiencies, making severity assessment difficult and subjective. This study proposes a color-texture feature fusion method to classify citrus leaf images into four HLB severity classes: healthy, mild, moderate, and severe. A dataset of 1,000 citrus leaf images from Sumanto et al. (2023), comprising 250 images per class, was used. papers.abstract: Ponderosa pine ( Pinus ponderosa ) is a foundational species in dry-forest landscapes across western North America. Ongoing warming and aridification intensify climatic stress across its native range. Prior research on ponderosa pine health is regional in scope and focuses on single disturbances, leaving the combined influence of climate, stand structure, and biotic agents on dieback and mortality poorly understood. To address these knowledge gaps, we surveyed sites across California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming during 2024 and 2025. At each site, we characterized stand conditions, assessed tree health, and collected tissue samples for pathogen identification. Long-term changes in climate were also recorded at each site to test associations between tree health and biotic and abiotic factors. Recent climate trends included reduced precipitation, elevated mean temperatures, and changes in vapor pressure deficit, indicating the potential for climatic stress on trees. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. papers.abstract: Background: Adults with a modified lower urinary tract (MLUT) represent a growing but understudied population in renal transplantation. Concerns regarding long-term graft survival, infection, and urological morbidity persist, yet adult-specific outcome synthesis and clinically useful guidance are lacking. Methods: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of studies reporting posttransplant outcomes in adults with abnormal or surgically MLUT anatomy. Primary outcomes were 1- and 5-y graft and patient survival. Secondary outcomes included urological complications. Given substantial heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively. Results: Twenty-four studies, including 511 MLUT recipients, were identified. Most were retrospective single-center series, and only a minority included comparator cohorts. Several studies included mixed adult-pediatric cohorts where adult-only outcomes could not be separated. papers.abstract: Abstract The growing demands for general healthcare and medical treatments have prompted the need for innovative diagnostic techniques. Ensuring proper and timely identification of invading pathogens remains at the forefront of this technological growth, paving the way for administering effective medication. Through the development of point-of-care (POC) systems, convenient and accessible diagnostic tools have emerged in recent years. Combined with localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) systems, the overall sensitivity, specificity, and applicability of these POC devices have undergone transformations, being able to reach a greater breadth of patients. papers.abstract: Oryza sativa (rice) is an invaluable cereal food crop worldwide. It is cultivated in a wide range of environments and conditions across the globe. Nonetheless, sustainability of rice production systems can be impacted by various biotic and abiotic factors, such as insects, pathogens, and weed infestation. Among these, weed competition is a major challenge as it can lead to significant yield loss in any cropping system, including rice. Herbicides have played a crucial role in controlling a broad spectrum of weeds.
